speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the nature of your pain; is it located primarily in your lower right abdomen or more centrally? Also, how many days have you had these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To narrow down the cause, are you currently experiencing fever or chills, and have you noticed any changes in the appearance of your urine or vaginal discharge? Also, when was your last menstrual period?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain and cramping. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Pain with urination, Burning pain during intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) with possible acute appendicitis or pyelonephritis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, CBC, and STI screening (Chlamydia/Gonorrhea). REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound.
